rounds.text: Taylormade Renewables Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.82x on a book value of ₹ 77.8 against a share price of ₹ 63.7 [E2], and key ratios place its P/B even lower at 0.74x compared to a lofty sector benchmark of 2.54x [E7]. This profound asset discount sits at the very bottom of the stock's 52-week range, positioned at just 1% of its yearly high of 248 [E5]. Beneath the recent cyclical noise of a 53% trailing twelve-month sales contraction [E17], the business demonstrates massive multi-year expansion power with a 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 141% [E15] and a solid 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 11% [E14]. Conceded: the company carries a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], a trailing P/E of 46.8x [E1], and a negative year-over-year sales screen reason of -42% [E67]. Yet the current market capitalisation of ₹ 79.0 Cr [E3] fails to capture the immense underlying asset cushion and proven historical growth velocity.

The valuation presents a heavy burden when judged against underlying earning power, evidenced by a trailing P/E of 46.8x from filed statements [E1] and a key-ratios P/E of 39.07x that severely outpaces the sector benchmark of 23.97x [E6]. Operational momentum has suffered a severe contraction, demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of -53% [E17] and a year-over-year sales drop of 42% [E67], accompanied by decelerating earnings growth [E68]. This deteriorating fundamental backdrop has already inflicted severe damage on market sentiment, leaving the stock languishing merely 1% up from its 52-week low within a range spanning up to 248 [E5]. Furthermore, expectations have historically outpaced actual delivery, marked by a price-led signal where price growth exceeds profit growth by 12% [E55], while income-seeking investors receive no compensation given the 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits attractively below the sector benchmark at 0.74x compared to 2.54x [E7], and the five-year compounded sales growth reached an impressive 141% [E15].

Conceded: trailing P/E of 46.8x [E1] and 39.07x against the 23.97x sector benchmark [E6], alongside zero dividend yield [E4]. However, the market cap of ₹ 79.0 Cr [E3] completely misprices a business capable of massive multi-year expansion, proven by a phenomenal 141% compounded sales growth over 5 years [E15]. The stock sitting only 1% above its 52-week low of 62 within a high of 248 [E5] reflects extreme overreaction rather than structural failure, offering deep value at a price-to-book of 0.82x [E2] or 0.74x versus a lofty 2.54x sector benchmark [E7]. The short-term sales contraction of -53% [E17] and -42% YoY [E67] ignores the structural 11% 10-year sales growth [E14] and 19% 3-year sales growth [E16]. Finally, the price-led signal showing price growth exceeding profit growth by 12% [E55] is fully neutralized by the depressed valuation and deep discount to book value [E2], rendering the bear's narrative of terminal decline entirely unfounded.

Conceded: the 5-year compounded sales growth of 141% [E15]. However, the bull's dismissal of the -53% TTM sales contraction [E17] and -42% YoY sales drop [E67] ignores a catastrophic growth collapse that directly drives the decelerating earnings [E68]. While the stock sits at 1% of its 52-week range [E5] and trades at a price-to-book of 0.82x [E2], this discount is justified by a lagging return on assets of 1.17% compared to the 4.92% sector benchmark [E8], proving assets are generating negligible returns. The bull's reliance on a price-to-book of 0.74x against a sector benchmark of 2.54x [E7] ignores that a P/E of 46.8 [E1] and 39.07x against the 23.97x sector benchmark [E6] penalizes the equity despite the headline book value discount. Furthermore, the claim that price growth exceeding profit growth by 12% [E55] is neutralized by deep discounts is contradicted by the evidence that expectations are running ahead of actual delivery against worsening top-line reality.
